_: The home table of route places (16k type 10, standard 18): a stretch of a major road built as one place, its crossings and its road dressing, between built places or a built place and a city. A route place has no catalogue record; this row is its record. worldgen.blueprint.catalogue_ids() reads its ids. `structures[]` lists one structure of each route-structure kind the exemplar set proves and who builds it: `this-place` (laid in this place's layout with the modular-runs rules, decision 0115), `route-compile` (a stair, lip step or stepped ascent of world/sources/routes/route-structures.json, built by worldgen.compile_route_structures), or another place id (a ferry crossing inside a settlement). A kind not on this stretch is `pending: packet` with the stretch that holds it.

places.name: the Border road crossings below Greenspring
places.why: West of the Greenspring track the Border road drops off the ridge into the marsh where an inlet stream meets the river. It crosses the inlet mouth and then a reach of the river marsh, each about half a metre to a metre and a quarter deep. The road was laid on a Dunmer line and its keepers carry it over both on piled timber, then climb the river bank on old stone steps.

structures.pendingWhy: not on this stretch: it stands 480 m east of Greenspring inside the Two-Gate Bridge's ground, which places it when that place is built
